topic: Four-slice ATT recovery on an absorbing Markov face. Observe iid five-date panels on states {a,b,e}, e absorbing, with treatment adoption at date 3, two known latent types, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths, no anticipation, cohort/type overlap, and common type-specific untreated transitions. On the declared face with no date-1 absorption, four nonsingular matched active-state slices, simple cycle-product spectrum, nonzero stochastic normalizations, separated common untreated cross-ratios, and buffered variance margins, prove that spectral projectors and row-sum normalization recover type masses, the component path law through date 3, and type-specific plus aggregate first-post state ATTs over the full compatible fiber. Derive guarded empirical-cell plug-in, the saturated finite-multinomial canonical gradient, and uniform Gaussian-multiplier bands. Use the exact H1,H2,Q1,Q2,V1,V2 witness with K=[[29/5,-12/5],[8/5,1/5]], type exit ATTs (-1/25,1/20), aggregate 1/200, and the initial-absorption counterexample. Distinguish Ahn–Kasahara, Markov-mixture reconstruction, Deaner–Ku, and restricted-HMM results; Rao–Risch is the interpretation consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Four matched slices yield K=B_a diag(rho_1,rho_2) B_a^-1; projector normalization B_a=[P_1m_a,P_2m_a], terminal row sums, full-row-rank pseudoinverses, and the no-initial-absorption condition then recover all promised factors. Exact enumeration reproduces state-vector ATTs (1/25,0,-1/25) and (-1/40,-1/40,1/20), aggregate (3/400,-1/80,1/200), while an outside-face construction preserves active slices but changes type effects. Differential recurrences and compact-margin Taylor bounds were derived, with numerical derivatives agreeing to relative error 3.7e-10. Checks covered scaling, equal weights, time variation, pseudoinverses, mass normalization, cohort labels, singular boundaries, support deletion, and neighboring literature; no collision or identification failure survived. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Verify Gaussian-max quantile continuity uniformly over the compact margin class, including singular correlation limits, and combine it with the buffered empirical guard; standard bounded triangular-array CLT and finite-multinomial information steps remain explicit compressions. EARLY KILL TEST: Run the draft's exact witness verifier, differentiate its recovery map on the 120-cell support face, and test positive coordinate variances plus singular-covariance max-quantile continuity; failure of rational ATT recovery or verbatim coverage by an existing theorem stops the run. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_absorbing_four_slice_att_recovery.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Do four matched active-state slices, spectral projectors, terminal row sums, and no date-1 absorption suffice to identify two type-specific Markov path laws and first-post state ATTs on a three-state absorbing support face?

source_refs.claim: Proposition 14 recovers finite latent-type Markov laws from short panels under nonsingular slice and positivity conditions, but its assumptions exclude the absorbing structural-zero face.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: Finite mixtures of first-order Markov processes are recovered from short histories under full-rank component conditions that fail at an absorbing cut.
source_refs.author: Ayden Higgins and Koen Jochmans

source_refs.claim: Spectral reconstruction from exact three-trail probabilities requires nondegeneracy and at least twice as many observable states as chains, excluding two active states and two types.
source_refs.author: Rishi Gupta, Ravi Kumar, and Sergei Vassilvitskii

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest econometric recovery theorem already uses four-slice inverse cancellation and spectral normalization, but its terminal factors and transition probabilities are nonsingular and positive. An absorbing observed state forces an identical deterministic terminal row and structural zeros, while deleting that state produces substochastic active rows and survival-selection reweighting. Existing Markov-mixture and restricted-HMM theorems therefore do not show that active-state projectors, full terminal row sums, pseudoinverses, and the no-initial-absorption normalization identify the full compatible fiber.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit observable projector-and-row-sum recovery map with a fiberwise uniqueness proof for type masses, component paths through date 3, and type-specific plus aggregate ATTs, accompanied by a compatible counterexample when date-1 absorption is allowed.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest motivation from categorical event studies to latent-type transition recovery and makes the excluded support boundary visible.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Discrete outcomes make linear trend restrictions incoherent -> transition laws supply causal counterfactual dynamics -> latent transition heterogeneity requires finite-mixture recovery -> absorbing structural zeros require a support-face recovery theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use multilinear Markov factorizations and simultaneous spectral decompositions to align labels and recover mixing weights, initial laws, and transitions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the same short-history mixture-reconstruction problem, while the destination must replace full-rank terminal matrices by active minors and stochastic row-sum normalization.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate simultaneous-diagonalization weights, express component moments as weighted empirical averages, and differentiate that construction for regular asymptotics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once support-face recovery is written as a smooth spectral map, it supplies the nearest estimator-and-limit template for recovered component functionals.

open_problems.open_problem: Can guarded empirical-cell plug-in and Gaussian-multiplier bands be proved uniformly valid on a compact absorbing face when the ATT covariance may be singular but every reported coordinate variance is positive?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves pointwise asymptotic normality under interior probabilities and nonsingular Fisher information and implements studentized weighted-bootstrap simultaneous intervals.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: Gaussian approximation and Gaussian-multiplier bootstrap bounds are proved for maxima of sums without restricting coordinate correlations.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

source_refs.claim: Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration bounds allow arbitrary covariance matrices when coordinate variances remain positive.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

open_problems.why_unsolved: The Gaussian-max and singular-correlation ingredients are largely available from Chernozhukov–Chetverikov–Kato, so max-quantile continuity is not a standalone literature gap. The missing proof is their integration with a rational spectral-projector map that is evaluated only after data-dependent determinant, eigengap, normalization, and variance guards. Ahn–Kasahara's pointwise interior MLE theory neither covers structural zeros nor shows that guard failures and Taylor remainders vanish uniformly over the buffered face.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform canonical-gradient expansion for the guarded finite-multinomial plug-in, uniform covariance consistency and guard acceptance, and a simultaneous coverage theorem for multiplier critical values along every positive-diagonal covariance sequence, including singular limits.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents the closest causal estimands and already motivates joint uncertainty across type-specific and aggregate ATT coordinates.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent transition recovery identifies state ATTs -> practitioners need joint uncertainty statements -> interior MLE theory yields pointwise Gaussian limits -> structural zeros and empirical guards require a uniform boundary-valid band theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple the standardized influence-function maximum to a same-covariance Gaussian maximum and approximate it conditionally by Gaussian multipliers with explicit covariance-error control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After guard-uniform linearization, the reported ATT coordinates are a finite maximum of sums of bounded multinomial influence vectors.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Gaussian comparison with anti-concentration to turn covariance convergence into distribution and quantile control without an invertible correlation matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is precisely the singular-correlation max-quantile step once coordinate variances are buffered away from zero.

open_problems.open_problem: If date-1 absorption is allowed, what are the sharp type-specific and aggregate first-post state ATT bounds over every stochastic two-type Markov factorization reproducing the five-date panel law?

source_refs.claim: Point identification and regular estimation rely on rank and interior-probability conditions that exclude absorbing structural-zero allocations at the initial recovery cut.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: ATTs for binary absorbing outcomes are identified under exact common-dynamics or proportional-hazard restrictions, without latent multi-state type recovery.
source_refs.author: Ben Deaner and Hyejin Ku

source_refs.excerpt: the bounded affine fiber used in partial-identification statements

open_problems.why_unsolved: Initial absorbers never enter the active slices, so their latent-type allocation can vary while the four spectral inputs remain fixed; this destroys the normalization equation for type masses and conditional effects. Existing absorbing-outcome DID results impose aggregate hazard restrictions, while the legacy proposal's affine-fiber device does not impose the nonlinear stochastic Markov factorization. Sharpness therefore requires proving that extrema of the semialgebraic compatible fiber are attained by valid component laws, not merely displaying two observationally equivalent decompositions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Closed-form or certified polynomial-program endpoints for every type-specific and aggregate ATT coordinate, endpoint-attaining compatible laws, and necessary-and-sufficient conditions under which each interval collapses to the no-initial-absorption point formula.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames absorption as a causal question about counterfactual transition paths rather than an ordinary outcome regression.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many outcomes terminate in an absorbing event -> level parallel trends is ill-suited to duration paths -> transition restrictions recover aggregate effects -> baseline absorption plus latent types leaves a sharp-bound problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode observed cells, stochasticity, absorption, Markov factorization, and the ATT objective as polynomial constraints and certify their global extrema.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination identified set is a finite discrete latent-variable fiber with polynomial equalities and inequalities.

method_exemplars.technique: Bias-correct estimated endpoint processes and calibrate Gaussian critical values with adaptive inequality selection for honest bound inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After an endpoint characterization, sampling uncertainty enters through estimated multinomial constraints and a nonsmooth optimized bound.

open_problems.open_problem: What joint decay frontier in the cycle-product eigengap, matched-slice singular values, and stochastic row-sum normalizers permits uniformly honest inference for labeled type-specific and aggregate ATTs, and where is localization impossible?

source_refs.claim: Identification requires distinct spectral quantities and estimation assumes nonsingular information, excluding local sequences approaching component collision or rank loss.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: Uniform tests and confidence sets are derived across weak, semi-strong, and strong identification regimes for extremum estimators.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Xu Cheng

source_refs.excerpt: characterize the maximal collection of rank-r sequences with Δ_K↓0

open_problems.why_unsolved: Every projector derivative contains an inverse eigengap, while slice inversion and stochastic normalization introduce additional inverse margins; allowing these to shrink jointly is not covered by a single weak-identification index. The prior survival-panel proposal left the analogous weak-gap phase boundary open, but its target is a linear pseudoinverse functional. Here the first changed proof step is to derive the local experiment for nonlinear matched-slice equations and determine whether aggregate ATTs remain regular after labeled type-specific effects lose localization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided local-to-singularity theorem giving minimax rates and limit laws in the three margin sequences, a thresholded-projector or test-inversion confidence set with uniform coverage in attainable regimes, and contiguous alternatives proving unavoidable width elsewhere.

writing_exemplar.why: It establishes the substantive role of latent-type ATTs while exposing distinct spectra and rank as the unresolved inferential boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Type-specific transition heterogeneity changes causal interpretation -> short panels separate types under distinct spectra -> weak spectra destabilize projectors and labels -> causal inference needs a joint margin frontier for aggregate and type-specific targets.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct drifting-sequence quadratic expansions indexed by identification strength and invert identification-robust tests for uniform confidence sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The shrinking spectral and normalization margins are identification-strength parameters for an ATT subvector.

method_exemplars.technique: Use high-order likelihood expansions around component collision to obtain nonstandard mixture rates and matching local lower behavior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same loss of first-order information occurs when two latent Markov components become spectrally indistinguishable.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply multiplier approximation and anti-concentration after establishing a margin-indexed asymptotic representation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The attainable side of the frontier ends in simultaneous inference for correlated ATT coordinates.

open_problems.open_problem: Under a declared observable tolerance on violations of matched-slice factorization and common type-specific untreated transitions, what are the sharp type-specific and aggregate ATT regions and honest bias-aware bands?

source_refs.claim: Transition independence may fail under anticipatory behavior or group-specific aggregate shocks; the paper proposes pre-treatment diagnostics rather than a sharp sensitivity region.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: Exact parallel trends is replaced by calibrated bounds on post-treatment violations, producing partial identification and uniformly valid sensitivity inference.
source_refs.author: Ashesh Rambachan and Jonathan Roth

source_refs.excerpt: Add an approximate-rank extension with a named, observable sup-norm projection-residual modulus

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact recovery uses exact simultaneous factorization, exact cross-cohort untreated transitions, and exact stochastic row-sum identities. Near a narrow eigengap or small normalizer, a small observable residual need not imply a small ATT error, and it may encode either transition drift or latent-mixture approximation error. Mean-trend sensitivity results are linear, while the relevant restrictions here are row-stochastic and propagated through a nonlinear latent Markov factorization; the first new step is a sharp perturbation-and-attainment analysis of that polynomial system.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For each observable residual radius, a sharp semialgebraic ATT vector region with endpoint-attaining stochastic factorizations, collapse to point recovery at radius zero on the regular face, and a uniformly valid confidence band separating sampling error from structural approximation bias.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates transition independence for categorical outcomes and names the anticipatory-behavior and differential-shock failure modes that a sensitivity model should quantify.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Transition independence yields coherent categorical counterfactuals -> latent types absorb stable heterogeneity -> anticipation or group shocks can still violate common transitions -> bounded residuals should replace binary specification diagnostics with ATT regions.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate finite latent-state compatibility and approximate transition restrictions into a polynomial program and certify globally sharp extrema.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Absorption, stochasticity, mixture factorization, and bounded transition deviations form a finite polynomial constraint system.

method_exemplars.technique: Index assumption violations by an interpretable radius and invert bias-aware tests for uniformly valid sensitivity intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired band is the transition-matrix analogue of honest inference under bounded parallel-trends violations.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one test one versus two absorbing Markov types and report aggregate-ATT confidence sets with uniform coverage across the type-count boundary, while recovering oracle width when the second type is detectably present or absent?

source_refs.claim: The number of latent types is assumed known; BIC, likelihood-ratio, or iterative specification procedures are suggested without post-selection ATT coverage theory.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: A modified EM test handles the nonregular null of one fewer component in normal mixture regressions and derives a simulable nonstandard null law.
source_refs.author: Hiroyuki Kasahara and Katsumi Shimotsu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Turn the unknown-rank OEQ into a two-sided testing theorem: state an explicit separation scale

open_problems.why_unsolved: Under the one-type null, the second type's mass and transitions are unidentified and the two-type parametrization is singular, so ordinary chi-square likelihood-ratio calibration and post-selection Wald bands fail. Existing mixture EM tests use smooth normal families, while Markov-chain order methods use different sampling regimes and do not propagate selection uncertainty into causal ATTs. The absorbing zeros add boundary constraints, and the prior rank-adaptation proposal shows that oracle width requires an explicit separation scale rather than consistent rank selection by assumption.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A one-versus-two-type statistic with a valid null calibration and local-power boundary, plus a test-inversion or projection confidence set for aggregate ATT whose coverage is uniform across the boundary and whose width matches the appropriate oracle above the separation scale.

writing_exemplar.why: Its known-type-count assumption and model-selection discussion make the causal consequence of latent-order uncertainty explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent types repair transition-independence failures -> their number is empirically unknown -> component-count testing is nonregular -> ATT inference must remain valid across the selected-order boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Reparameterize the extra component near homogeneity, expand a penalized likelihood to its first informative order, and calibrate a modified EM statistic by a nonstandard maximum law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Testing one versus two absorbing Markov types has the same unidentified-extra-component singularity, with multinomial path likelihoods and structural-zero constraints replacing normal regressions.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate chain count from algebraic ranks of trail-probability matrices before spectral reconstruction and control perturbations under noisy moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest order-selection mechanism constructed directly from Markov-mixture trail matrices.

open_problems.open_problem: At a repeated cycle-product spectrum, is the unlabeled type-ATT mixing law still identifiable and root-n estimable in Wasserstein distance even though labeled masses and type-specific ATTs are not?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior proxy result recovers a positive quotient effect law through eigenvalue collisions because observable moments are bilinear powers of one compressed operator. Four-slice Markov ATT recovery additionally composes projectors with terminal row sums, pseudoinverses, type masses, and treated-minus-untreated transitions. The first changed proof step is to construct a basis-invariant matched-slice functional equal to moments of the ATT law without labeling colliding eigenspaces; if no such functional exists, a collision may move the ATT law while preserving every observed slice.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observable recovery map for the quotient measure formed by type masses at type-specific ATT vectors, with a collision-uniform Wasserstein modulus and root-n confidence set, or a compatible observational-equivalence counterexample identifying the exact failure regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats the latent effect distribution rather than arbitrary latent labels as the causal object, which is the correct framing at spectral collision.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent heterogeneity is represented spectrally -> separated eigenvalues recover labeled types -> collisions destroy arbitrary labels -> ask whether the unlabeled Markov ATT law remains observable.

method_exemplars.technique: Use compressed-operator power moments and anchor bilinear forms to identify symmetric functionals of a latent effect distribution through eigenvalue multiplicities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination likewise needs a basis-invariant observable that discards labels but retains the quotient ATT measure.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze singularity order and construct local minimax bounds for finite mixing measures near component merger.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If the quotient law remains identified, component collisions determine its attainable Wasserstein modulus and estimator rate.

literature_map:
1. Ahn and Kasahara (2026, arXiv:2603.07914) is the closest neighbor: it identifies latent-type Markov laws and type-specific plus aggregate categorical-outcome ATTs from short panels under transition independence.
2. Its proof already uses four-slice inverse cancellation, spectral normalization, and label transport, but its positivity, terminal-rank, and regular-estimation conditions exclude an absorbing structural-zero face.
3. Higgins and Jochmans (2023, Journal of Econometrics, 10.1016/j.jeconom.2023.04.006) recover finite mixtures of Markov processes from short histories using full Markov restrictions and label alignment.
4. Kasahara and Shimotsu (2009, Econometrica, 10.3982/ECTA6763) is a foundational dynamic-discrete-choice mixture anchor, while later work clarifies the additional conditions needed for global label alignment.
5. Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016, NeurIPS) give spectral trail reconstruction under nondegeneracy and a state-count restriction; Spaeh and Tsourakakis (2023, WWW) treat disconnected chains and unknown chain count.
6. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017, Journal of Econometrics) provide simultaneous-diagonalization estimation and regular limit theory for nonexchangeable latent models.
7. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009, Annals of Statistics) use Kruskal arguments for generic latent-structure identification, underscoring the difference between generic recovery and a declared support-face theorem.
8. Gassiat, Cleynen, and Robin (2016) and Alexandrovich, Holzmann, and Leister (2016, Biometrika) identify restricted HMMs under full-rank, ergodic, or independent-emission conditions that an observed absorbing row violates.
9. Those HMM results also do not connect recovered components to treatment counterfactuals or common untreated transition restrictions across cohorts.
10. Deaner and Ku (2026, arXiv:2405.05220) study binary absorbing outcomes through common-dynamics or proportional-hazard restrictions, but not multi-state latent-type recovery.
11. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, Annals of Statistics; 2015, PTRF) cover Gaussian maxima and multiplier approximation with arbitrary correlations and positive marginal variances.
12. Singular ATT correlation is therefore not itself a literature gap; the live proof boundary is uniform guarded linearization and covariance/quantile integration for the absorbing-face spectral map.
13. Andrews and Cheng (2012, Econometrica) and Ho et al. (2022, AISTATS) show why shrinking identification and component separation yield nonstandard regimes, but not for Markov-mixture causal targets.
14. Rambachan and Roth (2023, Review of Economic Studies) and Duarte et al. (2023, JASA) supply sensitivity-inference and polynomial-bound tools for approximate transitions and initial-absorption fibers.
15. Kasahara and Shimotsu (2015, JASA) and Lehéricy's HMM-order work address component-count nonregularity or consistency, but no scanned result couples absorbing-Markov type selection to uniform post-selection ATT coverage.
